stages.stranger: Oliver Hayes, hello, sorry. I was an optician in Bristol, and up here I heal people with light through a lens. It's less strange than it sounds.
stages.acquaintance: Clifton, in Bristol, up the hill by the suspension bridge. I had a little shop with a green door, a test chart, and a cat who slept in the frames display. I sang in a choir on Thursdays, badly, at the back, which is where they put me.
stages.companion: My dad lost his sight to glaucoma when I was fifteen. Nobody caught it in time, and it was entirely catchable. That's why I became an optician, really. He used to ask me to describe things to him, and I got very good at it.
stages.friend: The lensmaster's apprentice is going blind from the crystal light, the same slow way my dad did, and the Aetherians don't think anything can be done. I think I can make her a pair of glasses, but I need a lens cut from crystal deep in the Keel. Will you help me get it? I can't do this one wrong.
stages.sworn: She can see. She put the glasses on and read the lens-plates across the workshop, and then she cried, and so did I, and so did the lensmaster, who'll deny it. That night I told her about my dad, and she asked me to describe Bristol to her. I did, for two hours.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to help fetch a crystal lens from deep in the Keel.

options.text: We'll get the lens, and she'll see. I promise.
options.reply: Thank you, honestly, thank you. I'll bring the callipers, you bring everything else.

options.text: The Aetherians said nothing can be done.
options.reply: They said that about my dad, too. I'd rather try and be wrong.

moments.prompt: At the end of your first run he's peering into everyone's eyes with a little torch.
moments.line: Sorry, I'm just checking pupils, it's a habit. Look at my finger, please.

options.reply: Lovely, perfectly reactive. You've good eyes, you know.

options.text: Get that torch out of my face.
options.reply: Sorry, sorry, of course. Tell me if anything goes blurry.

lines.bored_warning: We've been rather idle, haven't we? I'd quite like something to do, if that's all right.
lines.leaving_good: That was really good, thank you, everyone. I'm going back to Lenswatch to grind some lenses.
lines.leaving_bored: It's terribly quiet, and the workshop at Lenswatch has a backlog. I'll pop back, if you don't mind.
lines.after_wipe: Everyone keep still a moment while I check you over. Then we can talk about it.
lines.wipe_warning: I'm sorry, but I don't think we can keep doing this. Once more, and then please can we stop.
lines.wipe_leave: I'm going to stop here, sorry. You'll find me in the workshop at Lenswatch.
lines.zone_warning: I don't want to be a worrier, but this is quite beyond us, isn't it?
lines.zone_leave: This is too much for us, I'm afraid. I'll be back at Lenswatch.
lines.gear_refuse: Oh, I'd like to keep that one, actually, if that's all right, because it's comfortable.
lines.gear_taken: Of course, please take it. I spent eleven years in a cardigan.
lines.gear_short: If anything protective comes up, I'd be awfully grateful.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, how kind, thank you very much.
lines.back: Oh, hello again, how lovely! The workshop's quiet and I'm free. Where to, then?
lines.send_word: Oliver has sent word from Lenswatch. The lenses are ground and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I'm so sorry I left without a word. Have a cup of tea with me and I'll explain properly.
lines.neglect: Oh, thank goodness, you're back. I'd been worrying, quietly.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, just once more. Then I really must get back to the workshop.
lines.on_break: Oliver is back in the workshop at Lenswatch. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.mail_yes: What a lovely letter. I'll make my way to {town} and find a seat at the inn, with a pot of tea on.
lines.mail_later: Right now I'm halfway through grinding a lens and I daren't stop. A few days, I promise.
lines.mail_see_me: I'd much rather say this in person, over tea. Do come to Lenswatch if you can.

town_arrive.text: Half the people in this town are squinting. I could do so much good here.
Is there anywhere that does a decent cup of tea?

dungeon_clear.text: Well done, all of you. Now, follow my finger, please, everyone.

boss_down.text: Sit down a moment, everyone, I'd like to check your eyes.

close_call.text: Hold still, the light's coming, it won't hurt.

zone_arrive.text: The light's different here, have you noticed? It's softer, somehow.
